messages:
jin: Quick proposal — we should factor the canary/fallback logic into a small "canary-controller" service that only outputs routing directives (variant, weight, ttl, reason) and evaluation signals. Runtime routers subscribe to directives and enforce locally. Keeps the router simple and makes rollout logic testable and auditable.

alex: Can you sketch why we need a controller vs. embedding the logic in the router?

jin: Two main reasons: 1) rollout logic evolves fast (safety checks, telemetry heuristics) and we want to iterate without touching the fast-path router. 2) We need a single source of truth for cross-region, cross-tenant rollouts (consistency + observability). Controller emits directives, routers apply them with the fallback contract.

kevin: Concern: session affinity + KV cache warming. If controller changes variant weight mid-session we'll churn KV caches and latency spikes. How do we avoid that?

jin: Agreed. Proposal: directives include stability hints: "affinity_window" (seconds) and "warmup_preference" (prefer pinned nodes). Router enforces affinity until hint expires. Also controller can emit a migration plan: phased lift of affinity per session-id hash buckets.

alex: That helps. What about rollback triggers? We don't want a noisy metric flip to flip everything.

tia: Suggest two-tier signals: fast health probes (p50/p95/5xx) for immediate canary cutover fallback with conservative thresholds, and slower quality signals (bert-eval drift, hallucination rate) that trigger automated throttles but not full rollback. The controller should support both with separate actions (emergency-fallback vs throttle-to-zero).

jin: Exactly. Controller outputs directives like:
```json
{
  "variant": "v2-quant",
  "weight": 0.05,
  "ttl": 60,
  "stability_hint": {"affinity_window": 600},
  "fallback_policy": "fallback-to-v1-on-5xx",
  "reason": "gradual-rollout-0304"
}
```
This keeps the router interface tiny: applyDirective(directive). Router is allowed to enforce local guardrails (per-node max concurrency, cache-affinity).

kevin: How do we handle multi-tenant rollouts? Some tenants want to pin variants for compliance.

jin: Directives should be namespaced by tenant id and allow tenant-level overrides. Controller keeps an override layer that wins over global policy. Also support explicit tenant opt-ins for new variants.

alex: Observability/forensics: need an append-only directive ledger (immutable events) so we can answer "why did user X hit v2 at time T". Controller should write directives + triggers to a durable store and emit traces.

tia: On the subject of long-term refactor: we should separate decision (policy) from telemetry adapters. Make the policy engine emit an intermediate representation (IR) of rollout intentions; telemetry adapters translate signals to predicates used by policy. That will let us swap out metrics without reworking policies.

kevin: Ops question: what about offline simulation? We should be able to run the controller policy against historic telemetry to estimate risk before committing.

jin: Yup — controller will have a dry-run mode and a "simulate-on-backfill" runner that replays observability. Also UI in console to preview expected traffic split and estimated cost/latency delta.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary-controller/0.3.0 deployed to staging @ 11:22 :rocket: (checks: smoke ok)

alex: Next steps: 1) prototype minimal directive schema + router apply API, 2) add stability_hint and fallback_policy fields, 3) bench session-affinity impact with synthetic traffic. I'll open a tiny RFC doc and link tests.

jin: I'll draft RFC and include migration plan for existing router logic. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
